title: self-serve-onboarding-and-experimentation-prd-2027-10-03
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This PRD defines the product scope, requirements, rollout plan, and success metrics for the Self-Serve Onboarding & Experimentation project. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-success for new developer signups, enable safe experimentation with feature gates and route-level controls, and provide deterministic economics during the trial period without issuing prepaid credits. This work spans the Redwood Console, API/SDK onboarding flows, billing signals, and the Optimize recommendations surface.

Context and motivation:
- Observed: >40% of new signups drop off before issuing a first production request. Qualitative feedback indicates friction: model selection confusion, uncertainty about costs, and lack of simple experimentation controls.
- Opportunity: Improve developer conversion by streamlining onboarding, introducing a creditless trial (trial consumption allowance tracked via soft quota), and exposing a compact experimentation toolkit for canaries, per-route fidelity controls, and A/B prompts.

Non-goals:
1. This PRD does not change enterprise Dedicated or Private contract billing semantics.
2. Not implementing a full-featured feature flagging system for customer-facing apps; scoped to inference routing and consumption controls within Redwood.

Goals and success metrics (OKRs):
- Objective: Reduce median time-to-first-success (TTFS) from 28 minutes to <8 minutes in Q1 after launch.
  - KR1: Increase percent of signups that make a first generation request within 24h from 58% to 80%.
  - KR2: Reduce first-week churn among new developers by 20%.
  - KR3: Enable at least 25% of onboarding cohorts to run an A/B experiment using the in-console toolkit.

Target users and personas:
- Indie developer / hackathon user who wants fast iteration and predictable cost for exploratory experimentation.
- Early-stage startup engineer experimenting with model variants and tuning prompts under low volume.
- Platform/DevRel teams evaluating Redwood for internal adoption, wanting a safe, repeatable experiment path.

User journeys (happy path):
1. Sign up with email/GitHub and land in the Console Quickstart.
2. Console prompts user to select a sample use case (chat, summarization, embedding).
3. User picks a curated starter prompt and selects a model variant preview.
4. The system provides a soft trial allowance (e.g., 100k free tokens or 50 embedding units) displayed as a dashboard meter and as a per-route quota.
5. User toggles an "experiment" control to create a two-variant route (baseline vs variant) and assigns split weights (60/40).
6. The experiment runs; metrics (latency, cost per token, quality pass rate on provided prompt set) are tracked in the experiment page.
7. At end of trial allowance, the Console surfaces clear upgrade paths and cost estimates for the user’s observed consumption patterns.

Functional requirements (priority ordered):
A. Quickstart & guided prompts (MVP):
  - FR-A1: A ‘Quickstart’ Console flow with 3 curated templates and one-click sample requests for chat/generate/embed.
  - FR-A2: On Quickstart completion, automatically preconfigure a demo API key with scoped, soft-trial quota.

B. Trial allowance & soft quotas (MVP):
  - FR-B1: Assign a trial allowance to new demo API keys (configurable: token/embedding units).
  - FR-B2: Soft quota enforcement: allow requests to complete but track overages and show warnings at 70% and 90% of allowance.
  - FR-B3: Telemetry emits trial_state events (granted, warning, exhausted) for downstream analytics and billing simulation.

C. Experimentation controls (V1):
  - FR-C1: In-console experiment builder for per-route variant definitions (model variant, max tokens, quantization profile).
  - FR-C2: Traffic split with configurable weights and duration; immediate preview of expected cost delta.
  - FR-C3: Auto-collection of experiment metrics: per-variant latency p50/p95, token consumption, quality pass rate on sample prompt-set, and error rate.

D. API/SDK support (V1):
  - FR-D1: Expose endpoints to create experiments programmatically (POST /v1/experiments).
  - FR-D2: SDK helpers in JS/Python to attach variant routing metadata and to fetch experiment results.

E. Billing & upgrade guidance (V1):
  - FR-E1: Usage simulator that projects monthly cost for observed test traffic at 3 volume tiers.
  - FR-E2: One-click upgrade CTA that converts demo API key into a standard billed key with optional reservation signup flow.

F. Permissions & safety (MVP+):
  - FR-F1: Experiments and trial keys are scoped to the org and the creating user.
  - FR-F2: Rate limits applied per demo key to prevent noisy-throat attacks (default 5 rps burst).
  - FR-F3: Abuse detection hook: escalate to support with automated short-term throttling if a demo key exceeds preset anomalies (e.g., 10x baseline variance).

Non-functional requirements:
- NFR-1 (Latency): Quickstart responses for sample requests should return within 500ms p50 for small prompts (<128 tokens) for hosted small variants.
- NFR-2 (Reliability): Soft-trial telemetry must be available in Console within 60s of request completion.
- NFR-3 (Security): Demo keys must be tagged and excluded from production audit export; any customer requesting formal compliance must opt out of soft trial usage.
- NFR-4 (Privacy): No long-term retention of trial sample prompts beyond 30 days unless user opts in for template storage.

Telemetry and observability:
- Events to emit: onboarding.started, onboarding.completed, demo_key.issued, trial_state.changed, experiment.created, experiment.metric.sampled, upgrade.initiated.
- Dashboards to build: Acquisition funnel (signup -> quickstart -> first request), Experiment adoption (experiments created/week), Trial exhaustion cohort analysis, Upgrade conversion by trial consumption band.
- Alert thresholds: if onboarding completion rate drops below 50% for any 7-day window, page Growth PM and DevEx oncall.

Security and compliance considerations:
- Demo keys never grant access to Private deployments or Dedicated pools.
- PII: quickstart sample prompts must not prefill with customer data; enforce redact rules in examples.
- For customers in regulated industries, the Console shows a modal explaining trial limitations and invites contact with Sales/CS for a restricted Private trial.

Pricing and packaging implications (analysis):
- Trial allowance is not reconciled as monetary credit; instead, it is a tracked soft quota. This avoids accounting complexity but requires clear UX to avoid customer surprise.
- If a user upgrades during the trial, prorated billing will be applied from time of upgrade; system must flag accounts converting from trial to paid for potential fraud detection.
- Recommend a new SKU: "Trial to Paid Conversion Pack" to simplify sales tracking (implementation: billing tags on upgrade).

Compatibility matrix and constraints:
- Compatibility: Quickstart sample models will be subset of hosted catalog (small/medium variants); quantized variants excluded from Quickstart for fidelity reasons.
- Constraint: Experiments must not span regions (all split traffic remains within the user’s selected region).

Rollout plan and risk mitigation:
1. Canary alpha (2 weeks): Internal devs + beta partners only. Validate telemetry and trial_state transitions.
2. Limited public beta (4 weeks): 10% of new signups routed to new Quickstart. Closely monitor onboarding funnel and support load.
3. Full launch: All new signups get Quickstart and demo key.

Rollback criteria (example):
- If first-request error rate increases by >3x in the canary group for 24h, rollback Quickstart traffic and raise incident.
- If conversion to paid drops by >10% in beta cohort relative to control, pause rollout and triage.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Product (Owner): Maya Chen — defines acceptance criteria and handles stakeholder alignment.
- Engineering: DevEx (implementation of Console flows & SDKs) — Diego Alvarez (eng EM).
- Analytics: Priya Nair — experiment analysis and funnel dashboards.
- Security: Owen Park — gating for demo keys and abuse detection.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Quickstart flow is available in Console and issues demo API keys with trial allowance.
- Experiment builder allows creation of a two-variant experiment and records metrics for at least 95% of routed requests.
- Billing upgrade path converts demo keys into paid keys and emits upgrade.initiated for analytics.

Appendix: sample API usage (illustrative)
1) Create experiment (pseudo-API):
POST /v1/experiments
Headers: Authorization: Bearer demo-<id>
Body: {"name":"onboard-chat-ab","route":"/v1/generate","variants":[{"model":"gpt-small","weight":60},{"model":"gpt-small-quant","weight":40}],"duration_days":7}

2) SDK helper snippet (JS):
const { createExperiment } = require('@redwood/sdk');
await createExperiment({ name: 'signup-ab', route: '/v1/chat', variants: [{model: 'gpt-small', weight: 50}, {model: 'gpt-small-rc', weight:50}], durationDays: 3 });

Related pages and references:
- product-docs/product-overview/onboarding-playbook-templates (internal)
- eng-platform/rollouts/canary-guidelines
- product-docs/requirements/predictive-batching-cost-optimizer-prd-2026-03-01.json

Notes and open questions:
- Q1: Exact size of default trial allowance (tokens vs embedding units) — recommended starting point: 100k tokens OR 25k embedding units.
- Q2: UI language for soft quota vs credited trials — run A/B test to select phrasing that reduces surprise.

Summary:
This PRD outlines a cross-functional program to make Redwood more approachable for developers by offering a guided Quickstart, a soft-trial demo key, and an in-console experimentation toolkit that ties to clear upgrade paths. The focus is on measurable improvements in onboarding conversion and on creating low-friction experimentation primitives that surface cost and quality signals early in the customer journey.
